fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is generic powder metallurgy rather than liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu.
It omits the selective removal of Ti-rich interdendritic channels, retention of an RHEA ligament network, and formation of the W-rich passivating interlayer.
The claimed thermal-conductivity and strength improvements are invented and unsupported by evidence.
Mechanical durability of the finished composite is asserted even though the target study did not directly establish composite strength.

The service boundary incorrectly generalizes to fusion irradiation and high stress; the relevant irradiation evidence was only 25 keV He+ screening of precursor dendrites, not the completed composite.
No supporting prior evidence is cited.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad W–Cu uniformity, interface, and thermal-transport problem and names spark-plasma sintering as a comparator, but it does not reconstruct the central intervention or its material precursor. Its processing window, particle-size and pressure values, performance percentages, and strength claim lack support. The proposed comparison could be made experimentally, but it is underspecified: it lacks matched composition and density controls, temperature-dependent thermal measurements, direct irradiation conditions, interface characterization, and quantitative defect criteria. The hypothesis is therefore neither an exact nor partial reconstruction and is too generic and unevidenced to qualify as a well-supported alternative.
